findings: The stated finite-K Cartesian canonical preparation selects the stiff limit, rather than a canonical ensemble imposed directly on the rigid constraint surface. Fixed COM and free orientation introduce only constant factors here.

The rhombus tangent metric has constant determinant. The four positive spring-Hessian eigenvalues contribute a shape-dependent transverse partition factor, giving density proportional to exp(-U/T)/sin(psi).

The torque readout is the intrinsic angular-element force at an externally prescribed zero-temperature geometry, so the calibration carries no thermal entropic torque. Its sign is -stiffness*sin(angle-preferred).

The independent reference constructs Cartesian constraint gradients, their normal Hessian, and the tangent volume rather than importing the oracle measure. Positive cutoff separates all selected shapes from the degenerate flat-loop limit.
